glossary.rating: The number next to your name in maimai, which is the total of your best 50 charts.
glossary.odds: Your chance of hitting the target in one play, based on how much your scores vary.
glossary.constant: The exact difficulty behind a level like 13+, such as 13.2, which rating is calculated from.
glossary.trait: A kind of pattern in a chart, like streams, jacks, slide chains or tempo changes.
glossary.newpool: Charts from the current version, where 15 count toward your rating.
glossary.oldpool: Charts from older versions, where 35 count toward your rating.
glossary.judgement: How each note was hit: critical perfect, perfect, great, good or miss.
glossary.dxscore: A separate score for how many notes you hit with the best timing, which doesn't affect rating.
glossary.curve: Your scores plotted against chart constant, with a line showing what you'd be expected to score.
glossary.confirmed: Shuffled tags beat it less than 1 time in 50, and it held up in both halves of your charts.
glossary.mainotes: A community site where people tag charts by pattern, covering about 1 in 10 charts, mostly Master and up.
glossary.notation: The chart file itself, note by note.
glossary.region: The version of the game you play, where International is usually about a version behind Japan.
glossary.sss: An achievement of 100.0% or more, one rank below SSS+ at 100.5%.

c01_login.name: /login
c01_login.what: Links your maimai account. You get a link, sign in at maimai DX NET and press one button. It takes about a minute and you only do it once. You need to do this before any other command works. International accounts link with a bookmark; for a Japan account, run /login region:Japan and sign in with your SEGA ID. Accounts from the Chinese version can't be linked yet.

c02_help.name: /help
c02_help.what: A short version of this page in Discord.

c03_invite.name: /invite
c03_invite.what: Add Rasmai to a server or to your account, and get the dashboard link.

c04_support.name: /support
c04_support.what: The link to Rasmai's support server, for problems, questions and suggestions.

play.title: What to play
play.p01: Picks are ranked by how much <rating>rating</rating> you'd gain.

c01_analyze.name: /analyze
c01_analyze.what: Your grind list. Each row has a chart, the score to aim for and your odds of getting it. challenge changes the targets. Easier lands about half the time, balanced one in four, challenging one in six and long shots one in ten. level limits it to a level like 13+, a constant like 13.2, or a range like 13.0-13.4.

c02_plan.name: /plan
c02_plan.what: Plans a route to a rating you pick. You get a list of targets that add up to it, with the odds for each and a running total.

c03_session.name: /session
c03_session.what: Tell it how many credits you have. Each one goes where gain times odds is highest, with warm-ups first. A chart only repeats if you missed it the first time.

c04_new.name: /new
c04_new.what: Charts you've never played that fit your level, with a guess at what you'd score first try. focus leans the list toward a trait you're weak or strong at.

c05_random.name: /random
c05_random.what: Gives you a random chart around your level.

c01_b50.name: /b50
c01_b50.what: The 50 charts that make up your rating, 15 from the <newpool>new pool</newpool> and 35 from the <oldpool>old pool</oldpool>.

c02_chart.name: /chart
c02_chart.what: One chart in detail. It shows your score, your predicted score, what each rank is worth, the chart's patterns, how to unlock it and a video. You can search in Japanese, romaji or English.

c03_charts.name: /charts
c03_charts.what: Browse charts by pattern or level, with your scores next to each one. Good for practising something you're weak at.

c04_recent.name: /recent
c04_recent.what: Your recent sessions, every play, your new bests and what counted for rating. play:1 opens one play with every judgement and how much it cost you.

c05_dxscore.name: /dxscore
c05_dxscore.what: Your <dxscore>DX score</dxscore> stars and the charts closest to the next star.

c06_progress.name: /progress
c06_progress.what: Your rating over time, how fast it's going up, and when you'll hit the next thousand at that pace.

c07_area.name: /area
c07_area.what: Your progress in each area of area travel, the next reward and how many plays until you get it.

c01_profile.name: /profile
c01_profile.what: Your skill level based on your own results. It shows your <curve>curve</curve>, the constant you're comfortable at, the hardest chart you've gotten an S on, and how accurate the predictions have been lately.

c02_profile.name: /profile
c02_profile.what: What you're good at and where you lose points. Each trait is checked against your own curve, taking play count and difficulty into account, then tested against shuffled tags a few hundred times. A trait is only marked <confirmed>confirmed</confirmed> when it's unlikely to be chance. Most tags come from <mainotes>maiノーツ</mainotes> editors. For untagged charts, Rasmai measures the patterns from the chart's <notation>notation</notation>.

c01_compare.name: /compare
c01_compare.what: Compare your scores with another player who has sharing turned on.

c02_leaderboard.name: /leaderboard
c02_leaderboard.what: Rating leaderboard for this server. It's opt-in, and server owners can turn it off.

c03_settings.name: /settings
c03_settings.what: Your defaults, whether Rasmai checks your recent plays once a day, whether it DMs you the results, and who can see your scores. You can also turn on a public profile page here.

c04_server.name: /server
c04_server.what: For server managers. Turns /leaderboard on or off for the server.

c05_news.name: /news
c05_news.what: For server managers. Posts new maimai news in a channel as soon as it's out, from Preformai International on Bluesky and X, and Maimai Official and Laundromai on X. A post on both sites only comes through once, from whichever had it first. /news subscribe opens a menu: pick a channel, tick the accounts you want there, and hit Save. Want news from somewhere else? Hit Add an account and type any Bluesky handle or X username, or paste a link to one, and pick one under Remove an added account to take it out of every channel here. Pick a channel that already gets news to turn accounts on or off, or pick an account under Send a test post to see its latest post show up there. previous sends that many older posts from the accounts you just ticked (0 by default). If I'm missing Manage Webhooks, you get a link to add it. /news unsubscribe shows every channel here and what it gets, and stops the ones you pick. You need Manage Webhooks to use either.

c01_refresh.name: /refresh
c01_refresh.what: Gets your scores from maimai DX NET right now instead of using the saved copy. You rarely need this, since Rasmai checks for new plays whenever you run a command.

c02_export.name: /export
c02_export.what: All your stored scores as a file. You can import the JSON again from the Account tab on the site. Choose kamaitachi for a file you can upload to Kamaitachi with Import Scores, then Batch Manual.

c03_delete_account.name: /delete-account
c03_delete_account.what: Deletes everything stored about you, including your account, scores and history. There's no confirmation email or waiting period.

website.title: The website
website.p01: <me>The dashboard</me> has everything the commands have, with more room. You sign in with Discord, and it only gets your ID and name.

u01.i01: Overview shows your rating over time and your curve with every chart you've scored.
u01.i02: What to play and New charts are /analyze and /new, with filters so you don't have to retype them.
u01.i03: Traits shows what you lose points on, what you're good at, how sure it is about each, and charts at your level to practise the weak ones.
u01.i04: Best 50, All charts and Recent are your scores with filters, sorting and search in Japanese, romaji or English.
u01.i05: Look up is /chart with a pattern browser, so you can find every chart with a certain pattern and practise it.
u01.i06: Areas and Account cover area travel, your settings, importing an old export or scores from Kamaitachi, downloading a file for Kamaitachi and deleting your account.

website.p02: You can install it on your phone as an app. Open <me>rasmai.lol/me</me> in Safari or Chrome and add it to your home screen. The icon shortcuts go to What to play, Best 50, Recent and Traits.

u01.i01: Rasmai only pulls from maimai DX NET when something changed. Each command checks your profile and recent plays, and uses the saved copy unless there's a new play.
u01.i02: Charts your <region>region</region> doesn't have yet are left out of suggestions. Look up still finds them and shows where they're playable.
u01.i03: If your score on a chart looks like one bad run, Rasmai suggests it again based on what you'd normally score and treats it like a first play.
u01.i04: Targets never ask for a rank you haven't gotten at that level before, so a 12,000 player won't be told to <sss>SSS</sss> a 14.

stored.title: What is stored
stored.p01: Rasmai keeps the following in one database file on the server it runs on. The first three items exist as soon as you create an account. Everything from your maimai region onward is stored only once you link a maimai account, with /login or from the dashboard:

u01.i01: Your account ID, so Rasmai knows which maimai account is yours when you run a command. For an account that uses Discord this is your Discord user ID. For an account made only with Google it is a random ID Rasmai makes up.
u01.i01b: Your sign-ins. For each way you sign in (Discord or Google): the provider, the stable ID that provider gives you, and a one-way hash of your verified email address, made with a secret that lives only on the server. The hash lets Rasmai recognise you if you later sign in the other way, so one person ends up with one account, and signing in with both Discord and Google joins them into one account. The email address itself is never stored, and an address the provider has not verified is not used at all.
u01.i01c: When you agreed. When you create an account you agree to this policy and the terms. Rasmai records the date and the version (a date) of the documents you agreed to.
u01.i03: International accounts: a maimai DX NET session key. This is the clal cookie the official site issues after you sign in on SEGA's page. It is not your password, and for an International account Rasmai never sees your SEGA ID or password. The key is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before it is written to disk.
u01.i04: Japan accounts: your SEGA ID, password and Aime card number. Japan's maimai DX NET has no session key Rasmai can borrow, so you enter these on Rasmai's connect page and Rasmai signs in to maimaidx.jp with them each time it reads your scores. They are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they are written to disk, are only ever sent to maimaidx.jp, and are never shown, logged or included in an export.
u01.i05: Your player profile as shown on maimai DX NET: player name, rating, title, dan and avatar, refreshed each time your scores are read.
u01.i06: A compact copy of your scores (chart, achievement, rank, rating, lamps and DX score) from your most recent read. It powers the dashboard, /compare and /export without re-reading the official site, and is replaced on every read.
u01.i07: Your play history. Every play Rasmai finds on the recent-plays page (chart, achievement, DX score, lamps, track and the time it was played), and each new best it finds on a read. maimai DX NET only shows your last 50 plays, so this copy lets the score graphs, /progress, the dashboard's Recent tab and the prediction accuracy check look further back. It grows for as long as your account is linked and is not trimmed.
u01.i08: Rating readings over time (rating, best-50 totals, chart and play counts, timestamp), one per read where something moved, so /progress can draw your rating over time.
u01.i09: Per-chart play counts, cached for 12 hours, or until you play the chart again, so Rasmai doesn't have to re-load hundreds of pages every time.
u01.i10: Judgement details and area progress. For plays whose judgement page Rasmai reads, the note counts and the fast/late split. For your map areas, how far you have got and when it was recorded.
u01.i11: Beta feedback. If you tell Rasmai whether a beta feature was better, the same or worse, it keeps that answer and the short note you may add (500 characters at most). The site's owner can read it, and it is not shown to anyone else.
u01.i12: Your settings from /settings: default layout, default targets and difficulty, and opt-ins that are off unless you turn them on: letting other people run /compare against your stored scores, appearing on /leaderboard in servers you share with the bot, a public profile link (below), a daily read of your recent-plays page (below) and a Discord message about what that read found. With the compare, leaderboard and profile options off, nobody else can see anything about your account through Rasmai except the anonymous totals described above, which never show who is in them and which you can leave with the Count my scores in anonymous statistics switch.
u01.i13: One-time login codes, stored only as hashes. They work once, expire after 10 minutes and are deleted within a day.
u01.i07b: Scores imported from Kamaitachi. If you use the dashboard's import from Kamaitachi box, the username you type is sent to Kamaitachi (kamai.tachi.ac) to read that profile's public maimai DX scores. Nothing else about you is sent. What Rasmai stores is the same as for any imported scores: the bests and plays are recorded in your history and deleted with your account. The username itself is not kept.
u01.i06b: Anonymous statistics. Your best score on each chart and your rating are counted together with every other linked account's to work out how often the people who play a chart get an SS compared with players of their rating on charts of the same level. This is on for every linked account unless you switch off Count my scores in anonymous statistics in the public profile box on the dashboard's Account tab. Your choice is kept with your settings. It is not a separate copy on disk: the bot reads your stored scores into memory and rebuilds the count once an hour. What is shown, on a chart's page on the site and in the bot, is only totals: how many players have played the chart, how many of them got an SS and how many would be expected to. It never shows a name, an account ID or any one person's score, and nothing at all for a chart too few players have played to hide who they are. It changes no recommendation, plan or rating. Switching it off only stops your scores counting toward other people's results.
u01.i14: Server news subscriptions. When a server manager sets up /news subscribe, Rasmai keeps the server and channel IDs, which accounts that channel gets (including any public Bluesky or X account a manager added), and the webhook URL it made there. The webhook URL is encrypted in the database and only opened to post. It's all deleted when the channel is stopped with /news unsubscribe or has every account unticked, when the webhook or channel gets deleted, or when the bot leaves the server. Nothing about the people in the server is kept.

stored.p02: Scores are read when you run a command, press the read-now button on the dashboard, or, if you turned on /settings history, once a day in the background. That daily read signs in with your stored session key (for a Japan account, your stored SEGA ID) and loads only the recent-plays page, so plays aren't lost between commands. /settings shows when it last ran and how many plays it found.

profile.title: Public profile
profile.p01: Only if you turn it on in the dashboard's Account tab, Rasmai gives you a link to a page at {site}/p/… that anyone holding the link can open. The link is a random code, not your Discord ID, and nothing on the page identifies your Discord account. It always shows your maimai player name, title, dan, name plate, region, rating, play count and rating history. Your best 50, recent plays, play style and area progress appear only if you switch each one on. The link also produces a preview picture and Discord embed built from the same data. Turning the profile off makes the link stop working, and asking for a new link replaces the old one at once. The name plate image is copied from maimai DX NET and cached on the server.

u01.i01: Dashboard sign-in. Signing in sets one cookie holding a signed copy of your account ID, name and avatar address (a Google sign-in has no avatar), valid for 30 days, plus a short-lived cookie during the sign-in handshake. Discord is asked for your Discord ID, name and email address. The email address is asked for only so the same person can be recognised, as described under what is stored. Rasmai doesn't ask for your server list and doesn't post anything. Signing out clears the cookie.
u01.i01b: Signing in with Google. Your browser goes to Google's sign-in page, and then Rasmai's server asks Google once for your name, your email address and the stable ID Google gives you. It does not ask for your avatar, contacts or anything else, uses no Google service after you are signed in, and keeps no Google token. Google learns that you signed in to Rasmai and is covered by Google's privacy policy.
u01.i01c: While you create an account. If you are new, the sign-in details the provider sent (including your email address) wait in a short-lived cookie in your browser for up to 10 minutes while you read the welcome page. It is deleted when you agree or after 10 minutes, and nothing is saved on the server until you agree.
u01.i02: Human check. The sign-in and account-connect pages show a Cloudflare Turnstile check, which loads a script from Cloudflare. Cloudflare also fronts this site, so it handles requests to it the way any content network does. Both are covered by Cloudflare's privacy policy.
u01.i03: Saved login (Japan accounts, optional). If you tick Save my login for next time on the SEGA ID sign-in, your browser keeps your SEGA ID and Aime card number in its local storage so the form is filled in next time. It stays on your device and is never sent anywhere until you sign in. Your password is never saved there. Unticking the box removes it.
u01.i04: Home-screen app. The site can be installed on a phone. Its service worker caches only the site's own static files (scripts, styles, fonts and icons) so the site opens offline. Scores, sign-in and API responses are never cached on the device.
u01.i05: No analytics, no advertising and no other third-party scripts.
u01.i04b: Your choices on this device. The language switch saves a cookie, rasmai-lang, holding en or ja for a year. The light or dark theme and the notices and install tips you have closed are kept in your browser's local storage. None of it identifies you and none of it is used for anything but remembering your choice. The cookie is sent to this site with your requests so the page comes in your language; the rest never leaves your browser. Without the cookie the site follows your browser's language.
u01.i04c: Links to other sites. The support link opens Rasmai's Discord server, and the footer's improve the translation link opens a translation-suggestion page on SimpleLocalize. Both leave this site, and what you do there is covered by their own policies. The site's translations are built into it, so nothing about you is sent to SimpleLocalize when you read the site.

u01.i01: Payment details. For an International account, also your SEGA ID, password and Aime card number: sign-in happens on SEGA's own site.
u01.i02: Your IP address. Sign-in attempts and reads are rate-limited with a short-lived in-memory counter that is never written to disk.
u01.i03: Messages you send in Discord. Rasmai only responds to its own slash commands and doesn't read chat.
u01.i04: Anything about people who have not created an account or linked one.
u01.i05: Your email address. Only a one-way hash of it is kept, and it cannot be turned back into the address.
u01.i06: Anything from your Google account beyond your name, email address and ID at the moment you sign in: no avatar, contacts, calendar or files, and nothing read afterwards.
u01.i07: The file from the dashboard's download for Kamaitachi button or /export kamaitachi. It is built when you ask from the scores above and is not kept anywhere.
u01.i08: Anything in the anonymous statistics' results that identifies you. Only totals are returned: no name, account ID or any one person's score is sent to the website, shown to another person or written to a log.

u01.i01: SEGA (maimai DX NET). Rasmai uses your session key, or for a Japan account your SEGA ID, to load your score pages from the official site, the same pages you see when you sign in yourself.
u01.i02: Discord. Rasmai's replies, including the images it makes from your scores, are posted to Discord in the channel where you ran the command, and are subject to Discord's privacy policy. Use commands in a private channel if you would rather other members did not see your results.
u01.i02b: Google, if you sign in with it. Google sees that you signed in to Rasmai, under Google's privacy policy. Rasmai sends it nothing else about you.
u01.i03: Cloudflare, as the network in front of the website and the provider of the human check, as described above.
u01.i04: Nobody else. Data is not sold, shared or used for advertising, and there is no analytics or telemetry. Apart from what you switch on yourself, the only thing other people ever see that comes from your scores is the anonymous totals described under what is stored.
u01.i03b: The support server. If you join Rasmai's support server on Discord, what you post there can be read by its members and is subject to Discord's privacy policy. Don't post your login link, SEGA ID or password. Rasmai itself sends that server nothing about you.
u01.i02c: Kamaitachi, only if you use its import or upload its file yourself. The username you import is sent to kamai.tachi.ac. Scores you upload there are under Kamaitachi's own policy, not this one.
u01.i02d: The news sources. /news reads public posts from Bluesky, and from X through public Nitter mirrors. Japanese posts are translated by a model running on the bot's own machine if one is set up, or by Google Translate if not. Nothing about you or your server is sent to any of them.

kept.title: How long it is kept, and how to delete it
kept.p01: Your account, its linked maimai account, scores and play history stay until you remove them, with one exception: if maimai DX NET stops accepting your session key (for a Japan account, your SEGA ID and password) and you don't link again within 30 days, everything listed under Yourself, at once below is deleted automatically. The dashboard shows the date while your session is expired, and two days before it Rasmai sends you a Discord message saying so, with a button to link again, if Discord lets it message you. Apart from that, nothing expires on its own except the session key, which stops working when SEGA expires it, and the caches listed above.

u01.i01: Yourself, at once. Run /delete-account in Discord, or press unlink on the dashboard's Account tab (or delete my account there if you haven't linked maimai). Any of them deletes your session key or SEGA ID sign-in, profile, profile link, stored scores, play history, judgement details, area progress, rating readings, settings, beta feedback, play-count cache, any login codes, and your sign-in records and record of agreement. Your dashboard sign-in cookie stays until you sign out or it expires, and it only holds your account ID and name.
u01.i02: How it is deleted. The same way however it happens: by you, by the operator, or automatically after 30 days. Every row stored under your account (your Discord ID, or the random ID of a website account) is removed and its space in the database file is overwritten, so it can't be read back out of the file, and the database's change log is written back and emptied straight after. Any copy the bot is holding in memory is dropped at the same moment, and so is your data in the one backup copy the server keeps from a past database upgrade, and in any debugging copies the operator has switched on. The one exception is the in-memory working copy behind the anonymous statistics, which is rebuilt from the stored scores every hour, so a deleted account drops out of it within the hour. Once it is gone it can't be restored.
u01.i03: By contact. If you cannot use either, for example because you no longer have access to the Discord account, your account was made on the website with Google, or you want everything about you removed including any record that you were ever linked, write to {contact}. Say which Discord account, Google sign-in or maimai player name the data belongs to. It's deleted by hand, normally within a few days, and you get a reply when it is done. The same address handles a request for a copy of what is stored, though /export and the dashboard's download JSON button give you that at any time.

kept.p02: Replies Rasmai posted in Discord stay in Discord. Delete them there if you want them gone.

u01.i01: Stored sign-ins (session keys, and Japan accounts' SEGA IDs and passwords) are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, which also detects any change to a stored value. The 256-bit key is derived with scrypt from a secret that lives only on the server, never in the database. Each sign-in is tied to its own account, so a copy moved onto another account can't be opened.
u01.i02: When a sign-in is replaced or deleted, the old copy is overwritten in the database file, not just marked free. Sign-ins stored under the older encryption were re-encrypted the same way.
u01.i03: A Japan account's SEGA ID and password are only ever sent to maimaidx.jp, over HTTPS, to sign in. They are never shown back to you or anyone else, never written to a log and never included in /export.
u01.i04: Login links are single-use, tied to your Discord account, and expire after ten minutes.
u01.i05: All connections to this site and to maimai DX NET use HTTPS with certificate verification.
u01.i06: Sign-in attempts are rate-limited and gated by a human check.

age.title: Age
age.p01: Rasmai is used through Discord and this website, and signing in needs a Discord or Google account, so those services' minimum age applies. It is not directed at children.

changes.title: Changes and contact
changes.p01: If this policy changes, the updated date above changes with it. When you create an account, the date of the version you agree to is recorded. Questions and deletion requests go to {contact}. This policy applies to the bot and to {site}.

what.title: What Rasmai is
what.p01: Rasmai is a Discord bot that signs in to maimai DX NET on your behalf, reads your scores, and suggests which charts to play for the most rating. It is an independent hobby project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by SEGA. maimai and maimai DX are trademarks of SEGA.
what.p02: The support server is a separate Discord community run by the operator. Its own rules apply there, staff may remove posts or members, and help is given when someone has time, with no promise of an answer. Never post your login link, SEGA ID or password there.

u01.i01: You may only link a maimai account that is yours. Attempting to link, access or interfere with anyone else's account is prohibited.
u01.i02: By linking, you authorise Rasmai to read maimai DX NET using your session, or for a Japan account to sign in to maimaidx.jp with the SEGA ID you give it, in the same way you would in a browser. You are responsible for deciding whether that is acceptable to you under SEGA's own terms for maimai DX NET.
u01.i03: Keep your login link to yourself. Anyone who has it before it expires can link their maimai account to your account.
u01.i04: You can delete your account at any time with /delete-account in Discord or delete my account on the dashboard, which removes what the bot holds about you. See the privacy page for exactly what that is.
u01.i05: You can sign in with Discord or Google. Signing in with both joins them into one account with one set of data. A person keeps one linked maimai account: if both accounts being joined have one, you choose which to keep and the other's maimai link and scores are deleted.
u01.i06: Creating an account means confirming that you have read the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy> and these terms and agree to them. Rasmai records the date and version of what you agreed to. If you don't agree, don't create an account. Nothing is saved until you do.

u01.i01: If you turn on a public profile, /compare or /leaderboard, you choose what other people can see. Anyone with your profile link can see it, so only share the link with people you are happy to show it to.
u01.i02: Beta feedback you send is kept with your account and read by the operator to improve Rasmai. Keep notes free of anything you would not want read.
u01.i03: A file you download for Kamaitachi is yours to do with as you like. Once you upload it to Kamaitachi, or import a Kamaitachi profile into Rasmai, that service's own rules apply to its side. Only import a profile you are entitled to use.
u01.i04: Unless you switch off Count my scores in anonymous statistics on the dashboard, your best scores and rating are counted, without your name, with other players' to work out how often charts get cleared. Other people see only totals from them, never your scores or who you are. The privacy page says exactly what is used and shown.

u01.i01: Do not use the bot or site to probe, overload or attack the service, maimai DX NET, or Discord.
u01.i02: Commands are rate-limited per user. Working around those limits, or running automated clients against the bot, is not allowed.
u01.i03: Do not misrepresent Rasmai as an official SEGA service.

u01.i01: Recommendations are estimates. Rating maths follows the game's public formula, but chart constants come from a community database and may lag behind or differ from your region. Odds and targets are predictions based on your own history and aren't guaranteed. The clear rates shown on a chart's page are for interest only: they reflect only the players who chose to play that chart.
u01.i02: The service is provided as is, with no warranty of any kind. It may be unavailable, change, or stop at any time, including if maimai DX NET changes in a way that breaks it.
u01.i03: Liability is limited to the fullest extent the law allows. The operator is not liable for any loss arising from use of, or inability to use, the bot or site, including anything that happens to your SEGA account.

stopping.title: Stopping
stopping.p01: You can stop using Rasmai whenever you like. /delete-account removes your data, and an account whose maimai session stays expired for 30 days without being linked again is deleted automatically. The operator may remove linked accounts or restrict access, for example in response to abuse, without notice.

changes.title: Changes and contact
changes.p01: These terms may be updated. The updated date above marks the current version, and the version you agreed to when you created your account is recorded. Continued use after a change means you accept it. Questions go to {contact}.

expired.headline: That link has expired
expired.detail: Login links work once and last about ten minutes.
expired.hint: Run /login in Discord again for a fresh link, or press “Link your maimai account” on the dashboard.

invalid_user.headline: This link isn't valid
invalid_user.detail: It's missing your Discord account info, or it was changed.
invalid_user.hint: Start again with /login in Discord, or from “Link your maimai account” on the dashboard, and use the link as it is.

maintenance.headline: maimai DX NET is down
maintenance.detail: Your Aime sign-in worked, but the maimai DX NET score site is down right now, so your session can't be checked yet.
maintenance.hint: Your login link still works. Press the bookmark again once the servers are back. The bar at the top shows when.

no_login.headline: Couldn't read your session
no_login.detail: You may not be signed in to the SEGA gateway yet, or the sign-in didn't stick.
no_login.hint: Sign out of the gateway, sign back in, then press the bookmark again. A Japan account links with its SEGA ID instead: run /login region:Japan in Discord, or choose Japan under “Link your maimai account” on the dashboard.

region.headline: China accounts can't be linked yet
region.detail: China's maimai DX NET only opens inside WeChat, and Rasmai has no way to sign in there yet, so this login can't finish however many times you try.
region.hint: International and Japan accounts can be linked. If you also play on one of those, run /login in Discord and pick its region, or choose it under “Link your maimai account” on the dashboard.

credentials.headline: maimaidx.jp said no
credentials.detail: maimaidx.jp didn't accept that SEGA ID, password or Aime card.
credentials.hint: Check them on maimaidx.jp, then try again. Your login link still works.

rate_limited.headline: Too many attempts
rate_limited.detail: Sign-in attempts from your connection are paused for a few minutes.
rate_limited.hint: Wait ten minutes, then run /login in Discord, or press “Link your maimai account” on the dashboard, for a fresh link.

upstream.headline: maimai said no
upstream.detail: The sign-in was read correctly, but the maimai site rejected it.
upstream.hint: The session probably expired partway through. Your login link still works, so sign in to the gateway again and press the bookmark.

verify.headline: One check was skipped
verify.detail: You need to pass the human check on the connect page before signing in.
verify.hint: Go back to the connect page, pass the check, then press the bookmark again.

unknown.headline: Something went wrong
unknown.hint: Start over with /login in Discord, or press “Link your maimai account” on the dashboard.

home.metaTitle: maimai DX rating bot for Discord
home.eyebrow: A Discord bot for maimai DX
home.title: See which charts to play next.
home.lede: Rasmai looks at your maimai DX NET scores and tells you which charts to play to raise your rating. You get the results as images in Discord or on the web dashboard, and you can look up any chart's patterns before you play it.

analyze.title: What to grind for rating
analyze.body: Goes through your scores and lists the charts where a better score would raise your rating the most.

difficulty.title: Pick how hard you want it
difficulty.body: Easier gives safer targets and Balanced gives the best expected gain. Challenging goes for bigger gains that are still doable. You can switch it from a dropdown on the reply.

plan.title: Plan your next thousand
plan.body: A list of targets that add up to your next rating milestone, with the odds for each and a running total.

session.title: Plan a session
session.body: Tell it how many credits you have and it plans each one, warm-ups first. A chart only repeats if you missed it the first time, and you can see how much rating the session could get you.

new.title: New charts to try
new.body: Charts you haven't played yet that fit your level, with a guess at what you'd score first try. Add a focus to lean toward patterns you're weak or strong at.

profile.title: Where you lose points
profile.body: Your scores grouped by chart pattern and compared to your own curve. It also shows how well the predictions have matched your new bests.

chart.title: Look up a chart
chart.body: Shows your score, the predicted score, what each rank is worth and the chart's patterns. The song's other difficulties and a score history graph are a button away. You can also browse every chart with a given pattern.

progress.title: Track your rating
progress.body: Your rating over time, how fast it's going up, when you'd hit each milestone at that pace, and how many credits the route would take.

check.title: Check your plays
check.body: Pattern tags show what's in a chart before you play it. After a play, the play log shows every judgement so you can see where you lost points.

home.linking: Run /login in Discord and follow the link. For an International account you sign in at my-aime.net, open the Aime authentication, then press a bookmark once, and Rasmai only gets the session it needs and never sees your password. A Japan account links with its SEGA ID and password on the next page instead, kept encrypted. /delete-account deletes everything Rasmai has on you.
home.dashboard: Sign in with Discord or Google to see your rating over time, how you play, your best 50, all your scores with filters, the same picks as the bot, and 40 unplayed charts to try.
home.phoneHint: On a phone, add the dashboard to your home screen and it opens like an app.

link.step3: Back in Discord, run /analyze to see what to play or /plan to plan your next thousand.

welcome.title: Welcome to Rasmai.
welcome.lede: This is the first time this sign-in has been used here, so there is no Rasmai account for it yet. Creating one takes a minute.

means.i01: Rasmai makes an account for you and ties this sign-in to it. From the sign-in it keeps which service it was and the stable ID that service gives you.
means.i02: If the sign-in gives a verified email address, Rasmai keeps only a one-way hash of it, to recognise you if you sign in another way later. The address itself is not stored.
means.i03: Signing in with both Discord and Google joins them into one account, so you never end up with two.
means.i04: Nothing from maimai is read until you link your maimai account yourself.
means.i05: You can have your account deleted at any time. The privacy policy says how.
means.i06: Agreeing records the date and version of the documents you agreed to.

welcome.agree: I have read the privacy policy and terms and agree to them
welcome.expires: This page is good for 10 minutes. If it runs out, sign in again.
welcome.alreadyBody: Sign in with Discord first and this sign-in is added to your existing account instead of making a new one.
welcome.already: I already use Rasmai from Discord
welcome.nothingCreated: nothing is created until you agree
welcome.readFirst: Read these first. Both open in a new tab.

merge.title: Join your accounts.
merge.lede: The account you are signed in with and the Discord account you just signed in with each have a maimai account linked. One person can keep only one maimai link and set of scores.
merge.fromLabel: the account you are signed in with
merge.explain: The maimai link and scores of the account you keep stay as they are. The other account's maimai link and scores are deleted. This cannot be undone. Either way, both sign-ins end up on one account.
merge.cancel: Cancel and go back to the dashboard

privacy.metaDescription: What Rasmai stores about you and how to delete it.
privacy.title: What Rasmai stores about you.
privacy.intro: Rasmai is a Discord bot that checks your maimai DX scores and tells you what to grind. This page lists what it stores, how long it keeps it and how to delete it. There's no tracking, analytics or ads.

terms.metaDescription: What you agree to when you use Rasmai.
terms.title: Terms of use.
terms.intro: Rasmai is a free, fan-made tool. By using the bot or this site you agree to the terms below. Creating an account on the site asks for that agreement in so many words.

notFound.title: Page not found.
notFound.lede: This page doesn't exist or it moved. Here are some pages that do.
notFound.home: <home>Home</home> to see what Rasmai does and how to add it.
notFound.link: Link your account if you came here from /login. If your link expired, run the command again in Discord, or press “Link your maimai account” on the dashboard, for a new one.
notFound.dashboard: <dash>Your dashboard</dash>, after signing in with Discord.
notFound.bookmark: Came from the bookmark? Connect links work once and last about ten minutes. Run the bookmark on the SEGA gateway page, not on this site.

commands.metaDescription: Every Rasmai command and what it does, with the maimai terms explained.
commands.title: Commands and what they do.
commands.intro: Hover or tap a word with a dotted underline to see what it means. Commands work in servers and DMs, or anywhere if you add Rasmai to your account.

support.stuck: Still stuck? <link>Ask in the support server</link>.

errors.signin: The sign-in didn't finish. Try again.
errors.google: Google didn't confirm the sign-in. Try again.
errors.identity_taken: That Discord or Google sign-in already belongs to a different account, so it can't be linked here.
errors.rate_limited: Too many sign-in attempts. Wait a few minutes and try again.

kamaitachi.title: Kamaitachi
kamaitachi.info: Kamaitachi (kamai.tachi.ac) is a score tracker for rhythm games. Send your Rasmai scores there, or bring a profile's scores here. maimai DX only.
kamaitachi.downloadHint: On Kamaitachi choose Import Scores, then Batch Manual, and pick the file. It holds your best scores and every play Rasmai has stored.
kamaitachi.importHint: Reads that profile's public maimai DX scores and keeps whatever beats what Rasmai has. Nothing is overwritten.
kamaitachi.added: Added {bests, plural, one {# best score} other {# best scores}} and {plays, plural, one {# play} other {# plays}} from Kamaitachi. Reloading…
kamaitachi.nothingNew: Read {seen, plural, one {# score} other {# scores}}, but Rasmai already has all of them or better.
kamaitachi.empty: That profile has no maimai DX scores on Kamaitachi.
kamaitachi.unmatched: {n, plural, one {# score} other {# scores}} couldn't be matched to a Rasmai chart and {n, plural, one {was} other {were}} skipped.
kamaitachi.badUsername: That isn't a Kamaitachi username. Use 2 to 30 letters, numbers, - or _.
kamaitachi.noSuchUser: Kamaitachi has no user with that name.
kamaitachi.rateLimited: You've imported a few times just now. Try again in about 15 minutes.
kamaitachi.unreachable: Kamaitachi didn't give a usable answer. Try again in a few minutes.

cohort.observed: SS or better by {rate} of {n, plural, one {# player} other {# players}}, {expected} expected for its level
cohort.observedInfo: This isn't hard data. It's how the players who picked this chart did on it, next to how players of the same rating do on charts of the same level. Plenty of things move it: who chooses to play the chart, how long it's been out, how often people retry it. Take it as a rough guide.
